newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar little changed vs USD, weaker vs Aussie.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar little changed vs USD, weaker vs Aussie.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed little changed from its opening on Monday after a session of narrow trading.
Dealers said natural selling predominated but there remains an overall expectation there would be more buying in the offshore sessions on fresh samurai and euro issues.
At 5.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) the Kiwi was at US$0.6942/49 compared with its 0.6943/50 close on Friday.
The Trade-Weighted Index ended at 65.59, down from its 65.72 opening, in response to the Australian dollar's run up.
The New Zealand dollar cross against the Australian dollar ended nearly three quarters of a cent lower at A$0.8665/79.
Exporters, who generally have been standing back waiting for better opportunities nearer the October 12 election, found the cross rate attractive today, dealers said.

Generally though, business was quiet and is likely to stay that way until later in the week ahead of Thursday's pre-election economic and fiscal update and Friday's Reserve Bank six monthly economic projections.

Of 10 economists surveyed by Reuters, none expect the bank to announce an easing on Friday. The economists expect the bank's forecasts to assume the TWI starting point to be 65.1 and assumed to rise at an annual 1.7 percent.
Dealers said that as long as the bank does not ease, the Kiwi will remain well underpinned by the high short-term rates.
